title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test/release workflows and improve cache hygiene
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Consolidate GitHub workflows to reduce duplication, improve cache key hygiene, and standardize node/matrix testing. No user-facing changes.
description:
Motivation: Our CI has accumulated duplicated workflow files for lint, test and release steps across multiple repos and years of incremental edits. This makes maintenance expensive and causes inconsistent caching behavior that increases CI duration. This PR consolidates lint/test/release logic into a smaller set of well-documented workflows, introduces deterministic cache keys, and cleans up legacy jobs used only for debug.

What this does: - Consolidate .github/workflows/lint.yml, test.yml and release.yml into a unified set of workflows with clear job names (lint, unit-test, integration-test, release-checks). - Add deterministic cache key function using repo, node-version, lockfile-hash, and job-specific identifiers to reduce cache misses. - Introduce cache cleanup script and scheduled housekeeping (ci/scripts/cache-cleanup.sh) to avoid stale cache growth. - Standardize node versions used in matrices to Node 18 (primary) with Node 20 optional for compatibility checks. - Improve concurrency/timeouts and add explicit needs relationships to reduce wasted runner time while preserving parallelism. - Update docs and CI docs reference in CONTRIBUTING.md and dev-infra README.

Checklist: - [x] Consolidate duplicate job logic into reusable composite actions and shared workflow templates. - [x] Add deterministic cache key and invalidate on lockfile changes. - [x] Add scheduled workflow for cache hygiene. - [x] Run full CI across redwood monorepo and redwood-helm-charts for two-green-runs. - [x] Update docs and add migration notes for infra teams.

Commits summary: - "consolidate: move lint/test/release common logic into .github/workflows/common.yml" - "ci: add cache key helper and deterministic hashing (ci/scripts/cache-key.sh)" - "ci: add scheduled cache cleanup workflow and helper script" - "ci: standardize node matrix to 18/20 and pin build-image versions" - "docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md and dev-infra README with new workflow names"

Files changed (high level): - .github/workflows/common.yml - .github/workflows/ci.yaml (unified lint/test matrix + release-checks) - .github/workflows/cache-housekeeping.yml - .github/workflows/release.yaml (trimmed to trigger-only-release-steps) - ci/scripts/cache-key.sh - ci/scripts/cache-cleanup.sh - .github/actions/composite/lint-steps/action.yml - CONTRIBUTING.md - dev-infra/README.md

Testing and rollout: This was validated by running the new ci.yaml across the monorepo and two dependent repos (redwood-helm-charts, redwood-model-registry). We required two consecutive green runs because cache-key changes can cause an initial cold run; the second run confirmed cache hits. Release workflow was exercised in dry-run mode and a staged rollout to ensure no unexpected gating changes.

CI notes: The first pipeline run failed due to a flakey integration test unrelated to this PR; the test was marked flaky and retried. After addressing minor ordering in the integration job the pipeline passed. All checks were green at merge.

Migration notes for infra teams: - If you reference old workflow filenames in third-party automation, update to the new common workflow names. - External tooling that parses workflow filenames should be updated to look for ci.yaml and cache-housekeeping.yml. - Self-hosted runner pools can continue using the same labels; no changes required.

Related: ENG-1254, ENG-1301.
